sections.title: Onboarding Process
sections.subtitle: Steps to hire in Burkina Faso

steps.title: Contract Drafting
steps.description: Draft local contracts in French complying with the Burkina Faso Labor Code and OHADA standards.

steps.title: Employee Registration
steps.description: Register employee with CNSS (Social Security) and the Labor Inspectorate.

steps.title: Work Permit (Foreigners)
steps.description: If hiring expats, process work permits through the Ministry of Labor.

steps.title: Payroll Enrollment
steps.description: Set up monthly salary payments in XOF and IUTS tax withholding.

steps.title: Medical Checkup
steps.description: Mandatory pre-employment medical exam by an approved occupational physician.

items.title: OHADA Compliance
items.text: Employment contracts must adhere to the Uniform Act on General Commercial Law (OHADA).

items.title: Fixed-Term Limits
items.text: CDD (Fixed-term) contracts for locals are capped at 2 years; 3 years for foreign workers.

items.title: Language Requirement
items.text: French is the official language; all legal employment documents must be in French.

faqs.question: Can I hire without a local entity?
faqs.answer: Yes, using an EOR allows you to legally employ staff without setting up a branch or subsidiary.

faqs.question: What is the typical onboarding timeline?
faqs.answer: Standard onboarding for locals takes 1-2 weeks; foreign hires require 4-8 weeks for visas.

faqs.question: Is 13th month pay mandatory?
faqs.answer: It is not legally mandatory but frequently offered as a performance-based bonus.

items.title: Labor Inspectorate
items.text: The Inspectorate is very active; all terminations must be filed to avoid heavy fines.

items.title: Holiday Pay
items.text: Employees get 22 days of paid leave per year plus ~16 public holidays.

items.title: Maternity Leave
items.text: 14 weeks of leave, with the first 6 weeks taken before the expected date.

steps.title: Gross Salary Calculation
steps.description: Ensure salary meets the minimum wage of XOF 34,664.

steps.title: CNSS Deductions
steps.description: Deduct 5.5% employee social security contribution.

steps.title: IUTS Tax Withholding
steps.description: Calculate and withhold IUTS (Income tax) at progressive rates (0-25%).

steps.title: Employer Contributions
steps.description: Apply 16% social security and 3% Apprentice Tax (TPA) on top of gross.

steps.title: Statutory Reporting
steps.description: Submit monthly declarations to the DGI and CNSS by the 15th.

items.title: DGI Authority
items.text: Payroll taxes are governed by the Direction Générale des Impôts (DGI).

items.title: Payment Currency
items.text: Salaries must be paid in West African CFA Francs (XOF).

items.title: Bonus Taxation
items.text: Annual bonuses and commissions are subject to standard IUTS rates.

faqs.question: When must payroll taxes be paid?
faqs.answer: Declarations and payments are due by the 15th of the following month.

faqs.question: Are food allowances taxable?
faqs.answer: Standard allowances are typically non-taxable up to specific limits.

faqs.question: What is the IUTS?
faqs.answer: The Single Tax on Salaries (IUTS) is the primary income tax for employees.

items.title: Pay Slips
items.text: Slips must be provided in French and detail all deductions.

items.title: Reporting Frequency
items.text: Most entities report monthly, though small firms may report quarterly.

items.title: Social Security Cap
items.text: Contributions are capped at a monthly ceiling of XOF 600,000.

heroData.title: Incorporation in Burkina Faso
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to Incorporation in Burkina Faso
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for Incorporation in Burkina Faso.

steps.title: Structure Selection
steps.description: Choose between SARL (Proprietary) or SA (Public) structures.

steps.title: Name Reservation
steps.description: Check availability and reserve company name with the Center for Business Formalities (CEFORE).

steps.title: Capital Deposit
steps.description: Deposit minimum share capital in a local bank to obtain the deposit certificate.

steps.title: CEFORE Submission
steps.description: Submit articles, ID, and certificates to CEFORE for RCCM (Trade Register) entry.

steps.title: Tax & Social ID
steps.description: Obtain NIF (Tax Number) and register with CNSS for employers.

items.title: CEFORE Priority
items.text: CEFORE acts as a one-stop-shop, significantly reducing setup time to ~25 days.

items.title: Mining Focus
items.text: Specialized regulations apply for entities in the gold and mining sectors.

items.title: Foreign Ownership
items.text: 100% foreign ownership is permitted for most commercial activities.

faqs.question: Can I incorporate remotely?
faqs.answer: Physical presence or a local Power of Attorney is required to sign documents at the notary.

faqs.question: What is an RCCM number?
faqs.answer: It is your unique identifier in the Trade and Personal Credit Register.

faqs.question: Is a local director mandatory?
faqs.answer: No, but a local legal representative is recommended for administrative efficiency.

items.title: Criminal Record
items.text: Directors must provide a clean criminal record clearance within 2 months of setup.

items.title: Professional License
items.text: Registration with the Ministry of Commerce is required for a commercial card.

items.title: Bank Account
items.text: A corporate bank account must be opened to convert the capital deposit.

heroData.title: Staffing in Burkina Faso
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to Staffing in Burkina Faso
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for Staffing in Burkina Faso.

steps.title: Market Briefing
steps.description: Define skills; demand is high for mining engineers, IT, and project managers.

steps.title: Candidate Sourcing
steps.description: Leverage local job boards like FasoJob and professional networks.

steps.title: Vetting & Skills Test
steps.description: Screen for French/English bilingualism and technical proficiency.

steps.title: Compliance Check
steps.description: Verify minimum age (16) and clean criminal record (Casier Judiciaire).

steps.title: Offer & Placement
steps.description: Finalize offers ensuring alignment with the collective bargaining agreement (CCN).

items.title: Brain Drain
items.text: Skilled professionals often migrate; offering competitive benefits is crucial for retention.

items.title: University Talent
items.text: University of Ouagadougou produces strong graduates in law and engineering.

items.title: Trade Unions
items.text: Union involvement is strong in industrial sectors; staffing models must account for negotiations.

faqs.question: What are the top job sites?
faqs.answer: FasoJob and Emploi.bf are the leading platforms for professional recruitment.

faqs.question: Is English common?
faqs.answer: French is dominant; English proficiency is rare outside of international NGOs and mining.

faqs.question: What is the typical notice period?
faqs.answer: Varies by level; usually 1 month for workers and 3 months for executives.

items.title: Minimum Age
items.text: Standard employment age is 16; hazardous work starts at 18.

items.title: Local Preference
items.text: Priority is given to Burkinabé nationals; justify expat hires to the Ministry.

items.title: Probation Period
items.text: Typically 3 months for professionals, renewable once.

heroData.title: HRIS in Burkina Faso
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to HRIS in Burkina Faso
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for HRIS in Burkina Faso.

steps.title: Needs Assessment
steps.description: Identify requirements for French-language support and OHADA reporting.

steps.title: Vendor Selection
steps.description: Choose between global providers (Workday, Deel) or regional specialists.

steps.title: Data Localization
steps.description: Configure systems for XOF currency and local IUTS tax tables.

steps.title: User Training
steps.description: Conduct bilingual training sessions for HR teams and employees.

steps.title: Phased Rollout
steps.description: Go live with employee self-service modules and automated pay slips.

items.title: Cloud Adoption
items.text: Increasingly common in larger cities (Ouagadougou, Bobo-Dioulasso) with improved internet stable.

items.title: Language Priority
items.text: Systems must offer a full French interface to be effective with the local workforce.

items.title: Mobile Accessibility
items.text: High mobile penetration means mobile-first HR tools see higher engagement.

faqs.question: Does data need to be stored locally?
faqs.answer: Burkina Faso's data protection laws allow cloud storage if adequate security measures are in place.

faqs.question: Can it automate CNSS reporting?
faqs.answer: Yes, localized HRIS can generate the necessary monthly social security files.

faqs.question: Is tech support available in French?
faqs.answer: Most reputable vendors in the region provide support in French.

items.title: Electronic Signatures
items.text: Qualified electronic signatures are legally recognized for employment contracts.

items.title: Connectivity Issues
items.text: Occasional power or internet outages mean offline modes are beneficial.

items.title: Employee Data Rights
items.text: Under the PDPA, employees have the right to access and correct their personal data.

heroData.title: Accounting in Burkina Faso
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to Accounting in Burkina Faso
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for Accounting in Burkina Faso.

steps.title: Chart of Accounts
steps.description: Set up the SYSCOHADA revised chart of accounts specific to Burkina Faso.

steps.title: Document Collection
steps.description: Gather invoices, receipts, and bank statements monthly.

steps.title: Recording Transactions
steps.description: Post entries in French using compliant software like Sage or QuickBooks.

steps.title: Reconciliation
steps.description: Perform monthly bank and tax account reconciliations.

steps.title: Financial Reporting
steps.description: Generate annual financial statements (Bilan and Compte de Résultat).

items.title: SYSCOHADA Standards
items.text: Accounting must strictly follow the OHADA Uniform Act related to the organization and harmonization of companies' accounting.

items.title: Fiscal Year
items.text: The fiscal year follows the calendar year (January 1 to December 31).

items.title: Top Firms
items.text: Exco Ciecam and SEC Diarra are leading local firms for complex multi-national audits.

faqs.question: What software is recommended?
faqs.answer: Sage is the market leader for OHADA compliance in Burkina Faso.

faqs.question: Is an external auditor mandatory?
faqs.answer: Mandatory for SAs (Public Limited Companies) and SARLs exceeding certain turnover thresholds.

faqs.question: Can I keep records in English?
faqs.answer: Statutory records must be in French; internal management reporting can be in English.

items.title: Archiving Laws
items.text: Accounting documents must be kept for 10 years to meet statutory requirements.

items.title: Tax Integration
items.text: Accounting data is directly linked to the E-SINTAX platform for tax filings.

items.title: Chartered Accountants
items.text: Firms must be members of the ONECCA-BF (Order of Chartered Accountants of Burkina Faso).

steps.title: Annual Financial Audit
steps.description: Prepare and audit financial statements as per OHADA guidelines.

steps.title: General Meeting
steps.description: Hold annual general meeting of shareholders to approve accounts.

steps.title: Trade Register Renewal
steps.description: Update RCCM filings for any structural changes (directors, address).

steps.title: CIL Notification
steps.description: Notify the Commission de l'Informatique et des Libertés (CIL) for data processing.

steps.title: Insurance Renewal
steps.description: Renew mandatory employee accident and civil liability insurance.

items.title: GDPR Parallel
items.text: Burkina Faso's CIL enforces data protection rules similar to international GDPR standards.

items.title: Anti-Corruption
items.text: Compliance with local ASCE-LC (Highest State Control Authority) regulations is vital.

items.title: Employment Quotas
items.text: Regulations encourage the placement of local staff over expatriates where skills exist.

faqs.question: Is Whistleblowing mandatory?
faqs.answer: Large companies are encouraged to have internal reporting mechanisms under mining and financial codes.

faqs.question: What is the CIL?
faqs.answer: The Commission de l'Informatique et des Libertés is the national authority for data privacy.

faqs.question: How often are audits required?
faqs.answer: Public entities (SAs) require an annual audit; SARLs depend on turnover and capital.

items.title: Commercial Card
items.text: Ensure your foreign commercial card is valid for any business travel and contracting.

items.title: Labor inspections
items.text: Burkinabé labor inspectors have significant authority to enter premises and audit contracts.

items.title: Public Tenders
items.text: Compliance with the ARCOP (Public Procurement Regulatory Authority) is mandatory for government contracts.

steps.title: NIF Registration
steps.description: Obtain your unique Tax Identification Number (NIF) from the DGI.

steps.title: VAT Configuration
steps.description: Register for VAT (18%) if turnover exceeds XOF 50 million.

steps.title: Monthly Declarations
steps.description: Submit VAT, IUTS, and TPA declarations via the E-SINTAX portal.

steps.title: Corporate Tax Filing
steps.description: File the Annual Corporate Income Tax (IS) return (27.5%) by April 30.

steps.title: Tax Audit Support
steps.description: Maintain rigorous records for the frequent DGI fiscal control visits.

items.title: E-SINTAX Portal
items.text: Nearly all tax declarations and payments must now be processed through the online E-SINTAX platform.

items.title: Incentive Zones
items.text: Special tax exemptions exist for companies in the Investment Code zones.

items.title: Double Tax Treaties
items.text: Burkina Faso has treaties with France and fellow WAEMU member states.

faqs.question: What is the IS rate for mining?
faqs.answer: Mining companies are typically subject to a 27.5% rate but have specific exploration incentives.

faqs.question: Is there a minimum tax?
faqs.answer: Yes, a minimum flat-rate tax (AMF) based on turnover is applicable if no profit is made.

faqs.question: Are foreign services taxed?
faqs.answer: A 20% withholding tax applies to payments made to non-resident service providers.

items.title: Late Filing Penalties
items.text: Penalties start at 10% for late filings and increase significantly for non-payment.

items.title: UEMOA Standards
items.text: Taxation aligns with the West African Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU) directives.

items.title: Statistical Fee
items.text: Expect a 1% statistical fee on imported goods.
